title: 5. Numeracy & Number Systems: Comparing Integers on a Number Line
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Comparing Integers on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine which of two integers is greater by using a number line.
questions.question: On a number line, which integer is greater, \(-3\) or \(2\)?
questions.explanation: On a number line, integers increase from left to right. The integer \(2\) is to the right of \(-3\), so \(2\) is greater than \(-3\). Therefore, the greater integer is \(2\).
questions.hint: On a number line, the integer farther to the right is greater.

questions.concept: Comparing Integers on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine which of two integers is smaller by using a number line.
questions.question: On a number line, which integer is smaller, \(-5\) or \(-2\)?
questions.explanation: On a number line, integers increase from left to right. The integer \(-5\) is to the left of \(-2\), so \(-5\) is smaller than \(-2\). Therefore, the smaller integer is \(-5\).
questions.hint: On a number line, the integer farther to the left is smaller.

questions.concept: Ordering Integers on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Arrange three integers from least to greatest using a number line.
questions.question: Which list shows \(-2\), \(0\), and \(3\) in order from least to greatest?
questions.explanation: On a number line, integers increase from left to right. The integer \(-2\) is farthest to the left, then \(0\), then \(3\). Therefore, the order from least to greatest is \(-2\), \(0\), \(3\).
questions.hint: List the integers in the order they appear from left to right on a number line.

questions.concept: Comparing Negative Integers on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Compare two negative integers by their positions on a number line.
questions.question: Which statement is correct about \(-7\) and \(-4\) on a number line?
questions.explanation: On a number line, integers increase from left to right. The integer \(-7\) is to the left of \(-4\), and \(-4\) is to the right of \(-7\). Therefore, \(-4\) is greater than \(-7\).
questions.hint: Picture \(-7\) and \(-4\) on a number line. Which one is farther to the right?

questions.concept: Identifying the Greatest Integer on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the greatest integer in a set by comparing positions on a number line.
questions.question: Which integer is greatest among \(-8\), \(-1\), \(-6\), and \(0\)?
questions.explanation: On a number line, the greatest integer is the one farthest to the right. Among \(-8\), \(-1\), \(-6\), and \(0\), the negative integers are to the left of \(0\), and \(0\) is to the right of all of them. Therefore, the greatest integer is \(0\).
questions.hint: The greatest integer in a set is the one farthest to the right on a number line.

questions.concept: Ordering Integers from Greatest to Least
questions.learningObjective: Arrange four integers from greatest to least using a number line.
questions.question: Which list shows \(-3\), \(2\), \(-5\), and \(1\) in order from greatest to least?
questions.explanation: On a number line, the greatest integer is farthest to the right. Among \(-3\), \(2\), \(-5\), and \(1\), the positive integers \(2\) and \(1\) are greater than the negative integers. Since \(2>1>-3>-5\), the correct order from greatest to least is \(2\), \(1\), \(-3\), \(-5\).
questions.hint: Place the positive integers first in decreasing order, then place the negative integers in decreasing order.

questions.concept: Identifying an Integer Between Two Integers
questions.learningObjective: Determine which integer lies between two given integers on a number line.
questions.question: Which integer lies between \(-6\) and \(-2\) on a number line?
questions.explanation: On a number line, the integers increase from left to right. The integer \(-6\) is to the left of \(-4\), and \(-4\) is to the left of \(-2\). Therefore, \(-4\) lies between \(-6\) and \(-2\). The integer \(-7\) is to the left of \(-6\), so it does not lie between them.
questions.hint: List the integers in order around the two given integers and choose the one that is between them.

questions.concept: Identifying the Least Integer on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the least integer in a set by comparing positions on a number line.
questions.question: Which integer is least among \(-10\), \(3\), \(-4\), and \(0\)?
questions.explanation: On a number line, the least integer is the one farthest to the left. Among \(-10\), \(3\), \(-4\), and \(0\), the negative integers are to the left of \(0\) and \(3\). Between \(-10\) and \(-4\), the integer \(-10\) is farther left. Therefore, the least integer is \(-10\).
questions.hint: The least integer in a set is the one farthest to the left on a number line.

questions.concept: Moving Forward and Backward on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Determine the final integer after moving right and left on a number line.
questions.question: On a number line, start at \(-3\). Move \(5\) units to the right, then move \(8\) units to the left. Where do you land?
questions.explanation: Start at \(-3\). Moving \(5\) units to the right increases the value: \(-3+5=2\). Then moving \(8\) units to the left decreases the value: \(2-8=-6\). Therefore, you land on \(-6\).
questions.hint: Moving right increases the integer, and moving left decreases the integer.

questions.concept: Ordering Negative Integers on a Number Line
questions.learningObjective: Arrange four negative integers from least to greatest using a number line.
questions.question: Which list shows \(-8\), \(-12\), \(-5\), and \(-10\) in order from least to greatest?
questions.explanation: On a number line, negative integers increase from left to right as they get closer to zero. The least integer is farthest to the left. Among \(-8\), \(-12\), \(-5\), and \(-10\), the order from left to right is \(-12\), \(-10\), \(-8\), \(-5\). Therefore, the correct order from least to greatest is \(-12\), \(-10\), \(-8\), \(-5\).
questions.hint: For negative integers, the number with the greater absolute value is farther to the left and is smaller.
